en: The Chapter on the Indivisible, from the Section of Puzzling Questions.
6. The Question on Demerit “Venerable Nāgasena, you say:
‘He who commits the destruction of life unknowingly produces more powerful demerit.’”
Furthermore, it has been stated by the Blessed One in the formulation of the Vinaya:
“There is no offense for one who does not know.
If, venerable Nāgasena, one who commits the taking of life without knowing produces more powerful demerit, then that statement, “there is no offense for one who does not know,” must be false.
“If there is no offense for one who acts without knowing, then the statement that ‘one who kills a living being without knowing produces a stronger demerit’ must also be false.
This too is a dilemma, difficult to traverse and difficult to overcome, which has come before you; it must be resolved by you.
“Great King, this was indeed spoken by the Blessed One: ‘He who kills a living being without knowing produces a stronger demerit.’”
Furthermore, regarding the formulation of the Vinaya, it was said by the Blessed One:
“There is no offense for one who does not know.
In this regard, there is a further meaning.
There is, Great King, an offense that is cleared by confession, and there is an offense that is not cleared by confession.
Regarding that offense which is cleared by confession, it was said by the Blessed One:
“There is no offense for one who does not know.
“Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! It is so; thus do I accept it.
This is the sixth question on demerit.
